The 24-year-old Russian forward has yet to play professionally in North America, but he was a standout last season in the KHL, scoring 66 points (31G / 35A) in 65 games with Minsk Dynamo.

headline: Tucker (lower-body) is considered day-to-day after leaving practice on Monday.
context: Tucker played his first full NHL season in 2025-26, scoring 17 points (3G / 14A) in 69 games, and hopes his role will grow in 2026-27. That said, the 26-year-old defenseman suffered a lower-body injury that will sideline him, at least temporarily, for a portion of training camp.

headline: Ovechkin is day-to-day with a lower-body injury.
context: Ovechkin is dealing with a lower-body injury, which has sidelined him during training camp, but it is not expected to be a long-term issue. The 41-year-old future Hall of Famer played 82 games in the 2025-26 season and scored 64 points (32G / 32A). The Capitals added notable offensive depth in the offseason, so Ovechkin, coming off a career-low 17:27 time on ice, could see his playing time dip even more in 2026-27.

headline: Blackwell is day-to-day with a lower-body injury.
context: Blackwell needed assistance exiting the ice during practice on Saturday due to a lower-body injury, but he could return before the end of the preseason. The 33-year-old bottom-six forward played 70 games with Dallas in 2025-26, scoring 15 points (4G / 11A).

headline: Lizotte (upper-body) is considered week-to-week and will not participate in training camp.
context: Lizotte missed training camp on Monday and is expected to be sidelined week to week due to an upper-body injury. The 28-year-old bottom-six forward is entering his third season with the Penguins and is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he scored 19 points (7G / 12A) in 55 games.

headline: Poehling (lower-body) missed practice on Friday and is considered day-to-day.
context: Anaheim will be without their 3rd line center for the start of training camp after it was announced on Friday that the 27-year-old would miss practice due to a lower-body injury and is considered day-to-day. Poehling is entering his eighth NHL season and his second in Anaheim after putting up 11 goals, 36 points and 94 SOG in 75 games played last year. Anaheim did not disclose the extent of the injury beyond day-to-day, so his status for Anaheim's preseason games and season opener is unclear.

headline: Moore (lower body) will miss the next 2-4 weeks.
context: Moore was expected to be a key piece of the Anaheim Ducks' defensive unit after they lost a few big names in the offseason, but will have to wait for his regular-season debut after it was announced that the 24-year-old is expected to miss the next 2-4 weeks with a lower-body injury. The second-year defenseman is coming off an up-and-down rookie campaign, where he had four goals, 12 points, 24 PIMs and a -14 plus/minus across 67 games played. His spot is now up for grabs on opening night when Anaheim takes on the Vegas Golden Knights on October 2nd.

headline: Lund (upper-body) is expected to be out for a month.
context: Lund was hopeful to make San Jose's opening night roster after putting up nine goals and 25 points in 37 games with the Barracuda (AHL) last season, but will have to wait after the team announced he would be out for a month with an upper-body injury. The 22-year-old last appeared in the NHL in 2024-25, where he had two goals and three points in 11 career games played.

headline: Musty (upper-body) is expected to be out long-term.
context: San Jose announced Thursday that highly regarded prospect Quentin Musty would be out long-term after he endured an upper-body injury at San Jose's Rookie Showcase. The 21-year-old left-winger was San Jose's 2023 1st-round pick (26th overall) and was expected to compete for an opening-night roster spot after putting up 21 goals and 45 points with the San Jose Barracuda (AHL) across 61 games played last season.

headline: Duchene (undisclosed) is expected to miss the first two days of training camp for maintenance.
Brian Dumoulin (undisclosed) failed his physical and is undergoing further testing.
Mats Zuccarello is day-to-day with a minor shoulder injury. He skated in a non-contact jersey today.
Kevin Fiala (leg) could rejoin his teammates on the ice in three weeks.
context: If he doesn't have any setbacks, he could be in the lineup by Nov.1.

headline: Kovacevic will be a limited participant in training camp as he rehabs from a minor off-season procedure in his right knee.
Bjugstad underwent successful surgery to repair a torn left pectoral muscle and is expected to miss 4-to-6 months.
Barzal (undisclosed) has not been ruled out for opening night.
context: The Islanders opened training camp by announcing that Barzal would not skate for two weeks to tend to an undisclosed injury, but they quickly lessened the severity of the issues, announcing that he could still be an option on opening night. The 29-year-old forward scored 72 points (19G / 53A) in 81 games last season. Whether or not he draws into the lineup on opening night, it appears his injury is not a long-term concern for the team.

headline: Jarvis (upper body) participated in some training camp drills on Thursday in a non-contact jersey.
context: Jarvis underwent surgery in late June to address a shoulder injury and was given a four-to-six month recovery timeline. The 24-year-old Jarvis is still expected to miss the start of the 2026-27 season, but his presence at training camp is an encouraging sign for the team. Last season, Jarvis scored 66 points (32G / 34A) in 71 games.

headline: Makar (lower body) made his training camp debut on Thursday in a non-contact jersey.
context: Makar has been battling an offseason lower-body injury that has made his training camp status uncertain. That said, his presence at training camp on Thursday, albeit in a non-contact jersey, is an encouraging sign for Colorado's superstar defenseman. The 27-year-old Makar is coming off a solid 2025-26 campaign, scoring 79 points (20G / 59A) in 75 games, and is fresh off signing a lucrative eight-year, $163.2 million contract extension ($20.4M AAV), making him the highest-paid player in NHL history.

headline: Seguin (knee) has been cleared for contact.
context: According to Stars GM Jim Nill, Seguin has been cleared for contact by his surgeon, and it's up to how Seguin feels from here. Seguin, who has been out since December 2nd, had 17 points (7G / 10A) in 27 games last year.

headline: Janmark (undisclosed) will skate in Oilers training camp.
context: Oilers GM Stan Bowman said that Janmark will skate in training camp as he continues to work his way back from an injury that has kept him out since February 25th. Janmark will likely be on the outside looking in of the Oilers' opening night lineup, regardless of how much his progresses in training camp.

headline: Regula (undisclosed) will skate in Oilers training camp.
context: Oilers GM Stan Bowman said that Regula will skate in training camp as he continues to work his way back from an injury that has kept him out since January 20th. With the Oilers adding Ryan Shea and Shakir Mukhamadullin this offseason, Regula's path to making the opening night roster is limited.

headline: Nikishin (contract) will not be at training camp on Thursday.
context: Nikishin is an unsigned RFA who has requested a trade from Carolina, so he will hold out of training camp while he awaits a new deal or a trade. The Hurricanes' bolstered their defensive depth recently by signing both P-O Joseph and Mike Reilly to one-year deals.

headline: Marchand (undisclosed) will miss the start of the regular season.
context: Marchand underwent an undisclosed procedure over the summer that will likely keep him out of the lineup to begin the season. The details are murky, but Panthers GM Bill Zito said he anticipates Marchand will be "back early in the season."

headline: Barzal (undisclosed) will not skate for the next two weeks.
context: The Islanders released a statement that said that Barzal will not skate the next two weeks due to aggravation of a prior injury that has caused some inflammation. The added that they expect him "back in the lineup as soon as possible." With the Islanders' season opener exactly two weeks away, expect Barzal to miss some games to open the season.

headline: Larkin sustained an upper-body injury during training and will not be skating when camp begins.
context: Despite the public trade request, it was reported last week that Larkin would be there when training camp opens, but his upper-body injury will keep him off the ice when it gets underway on Thursday.

headline: Thompson is considered week-to-week with an undisclosed injury.
context: Thompson, who was acquired from the Blackhawks in March, has never appeared in an NHL game and likely wasn't going to make the Rangers out of training camp anyways. When he's healthy, look for the 24-year-old centre to start the year in Hartford (AHL), where he had seven points (2G / 5A) in 18 games last season.

headline: Beaudoin is day-to-day with an undisclosed injury.
context: As the Rangers prepare to open training camp on Thursday, roster hopeful Cole Beaudoin won't be there. Beaudoin missed Sunday's rookie game against Philadelphia due to injury and remains day-to-day. The 20-year-old was a first-round pick (No. 24 overall) in 2024 and was acquired from Utah this offseason in the trade that sent Vincent Trocheck to the Mammoth.

headline: Foegele (undisclosed) will miss the start of training camp.
context: Foegele will miss the Senators' training camp opening on Thursday as he nurses an undisclosed injury. Head coach Travis Green said that Zub is skating and that he "hopes" it isn't long-term.

headline: Zub (undisclosed) will miss the start of training camp.
context: Zub will not be there when the Senators open training camp on Thursday as he nurses an undisclosed injury. Head coach Travis Green said that Zub is skating and that he "hopes" it isn't long-term.

headline: Guhle underwent surgery on his adductor muscle this summer and is expected to return in four to five weeks.
context: Guhle, who has missed 70 games over the last two seasons, will miss at least the first 7-to-10 games of the 2026-27 season after undergoing surgery on his adductor muscle in the summer. This opens the door for one of David Reinbacher, Adam Engstrom or Arber Xhekaj to play as the Canadiens' No.6 defenseman to open the season.

headline: Domi (lower-body) failed his physical and is out indefinitely.
context: Domi underwent surgery in May but dealt with complications and remains out indefinitely after failing his physical before training camp. The Maple Leafs rebuilt their depth to help deal with Domi's absence, adding Teddy Blueger, Nick Paul, Colton Sissons, and Brandon Duhaime this offseason.

headline: James (broken hand) is expected to miss the first two weeks of the regular season.
context: James broke his hand during offseason training and he's expected to be sidelined for the first couple of weeks of the season. This should open the door for the Lightning to take a look at some young players in the opening games of the season, before James returns to his bottom-6 role. The 24-year-old had 15 points (7G / 8A) in 43 games during his rookie season.

headline: Gourde underwent hip surgery in the summer and is expected to be out until December.
context: Gourde appeared in all 82 games last season, scoring nine goals and 19 assists (28 points) while playing a key role on the Lightning's checking line with Zemgus Girgensons and Pontus Holmberg. With Gourde expected to be out until December, he's expected to miss at least the first 26 games of the season.

headline: Tanev (abdomen) has been cleared to play as the Maple Leafs begin training camp.
context: The 16-year veteran only played 11 games last year and did not play after December 28th. Tanev underwent core muscle surgery in March and is as "healthy as anybody" according to Maple Leafs' GM John Chayka.

headline: Merzlikins (shoulder) will miss the start of the season and is considered out indefinitely.
Zucker (sports hernia) will not be ready for the start of the regular season and is considered out indefinitely.
Fiala (lower-body) is expected to miss the start of training camp and is without a timeline to return.
context: Los Angeles announced Thursday that Fiala had undergone a new procedure related to his initial lower-body surgery from last season and is expected to miss the start of training camp. The 30-year-old has no timeline for returning after putting up 18 goals, 40 points, and 147 SOG in 56 games last season.

headline: Domi (undisclosed) is expected to miss training camp and is without a timeline to return.
context: Domi's offseason was full of uncertainty after it was announced that he would be out indefinitely following lower-body surgery, and is expected to now miss training camp as the Maple Leafs preseason begins to start. The 31-year-old is entering his 12th NHL season and fourth in Toronto after putting up 12 goals and 36 points in 95 PIMs in 80 games played last year.

headline: Demko (hip) currently has no timeline to return to Vancouver’s lineup.
Huberdeau (hip) is not expected to be ready for the start of Calgary’s training camp.
context: Huberdeau has been out since February 4th of last season due to a hip injury and is not expected to be ready for the start of Calgary’s training camp. The 33-year-old has struggled since arriving in Calgary four years ago, averaging just 15.5 goals and 48.5 points after finishing above 90+ points twice while previously in Florida. Calgary is still hopeful to have Huberdeau healthy and ready for the regular season, but the 14-year pro is already behind the eight ball with the latest news.

headline: Janmark (undisclosed) will miss Edmonton's Training Camp.
Regula (undisclosed) will not participate in Edmonton's Training Camp.
Andersen (undisclosed) will not participate in Edmonton's Training Camp.
context: The Oilers are expected to roll with a three-goalie rotation this season, with Andersen joining Tristan Jarry and Devon Levi. But with Andersen not available for training camp, Jarry and Levi will get the first cracks at staking their claim to a larger share of the split. There's no timeline for Andersen's return.

headline: Savoie (undisclosed) will not participate in training camp.
context: Savoie finished the year strong, posting 19 points (9G / 10A) in 24 games after the Olympic break, but will likely start the 2026-27 season on the injured list. Savoie will not skate during training camp, opening the door for players like Isaac Howard and Trent Frederic to play more ice time in the early part of the season. As of now, there's no timeline for his return.

headline: Terry underwent surgery on June 9 to address hip impingement and a labral tear.
context: According to the Ducks, Terry's recovery timeline was 5 to 6 months, which would put him on track to return in early to mid-November at the earliest. Expect him to miss roughly the first 20-to-30 games of the season, which should hand Cutter Gauthier and Beckett Sennecke more ice time early in the season.

headline: Kulich (blood clot) expects to be ready for opening night in October.
context: In 2025-26, Kulich's season was cut short by a blood clot in November. Kulich was playing a key role for the Sabres and had tallied five points (3G / 2A) in 12 games before being shutdown for the season. This summer he said that he feels good and expects to be ready for Opening night on October 1st.

headline: Lundestrom had surgery on his Achilles and is expected to be sidelined until early-November.
context: Lundestrom suffered an Achilles injury during offseason training and underwent surgery over the weekend. The Blue Jackets said they anticipate the bottom-6 forward to return to th lineup by early-November, so expect him to miss at least the first 12-to-15 games of the season.

headline: Bedard underwent successful shoulder surgery and is expected to miss approximately four months.
context: Video was circulating last week of Connor Bedard going down favourably holding his shoulder at a skate and Chicago announced Wednesday that their star forward underwent successful shoulder surgery and is expected to miss approximately four months. The 20-year-old will likely miss the beginning of the regular season and is entering his 4th NHL season in Chicago after putting up career highs in nearly all categories in 2025-26, including goals (30), assists (45), points (75) and SOG (226).

headline: Tippett (internal bleeding) is expected to be ready for training camp in the fall.
context: Tippett missed games 2 through 4 of the Flyers' second round series vs. the Hurricanes due to an "internal bleeding issue" that he sustained during Round 1 vs. the Penguins. Tippett said in a statement that he is "confident for a full recovery and look forward to returning for training camp in September."

headline: Jarvis underwent shoulder surgery and is expected to be out for 4-to-6 months.
context: Jarvis underwent shoulder surgery after the Hurricanes' Stanley Cup win and will need at least four months of recovery. That puts him out until at least late-October to late-December. GM Eric Tulsky said "there's a very real chance that we end up with sort of an open spot in our lineup for a month or two for a young player to step in and get an opportunity to show what he can do." So expect Jarvis to be sidelined when the Hurricanes open their season in the fall.

headline: Robinson had knee surgery and will need 6-to-8 weeks of recovery.
context: Robinson underwent offseason knee surgery and is expected to rehab for up to two months, which should give him plenty of time to get back to 100 percent before training camp in the fall. Robinson finished the 2026 season with 18 points (12G / 6A) in 67 games and added eight points (3G / 5A) in 19 playoff games during the Hurricanes' Stanley Cup winning run.

headline: Fiala (leg) is expected to be ready for training camp in the fall.
context: Fiala fractured his left leg in the Olympics and missed the rest of the 2025-26 regular season. But following the Kings' first round exit, GM Ken Holland said that he would have returned by Round 3 if they would have advanced. That's an encouraging sign that Fiala will be fully healthy when the Kings hit the ice for training camp in the fall.

headline: Karlsson (arm) will not play in Game 6 on Sunday.
context: Karlsson left Game 5 with an arm injury on a hit from Sean Walker and did not return. With Karlsson sidelined for Game 6, the Golden Knights will have to shuffle their lines around. Either Brandon Saad or Reilly Smith will enter the lineup to replace Karlsson, and either Tomas Hertl will centre the second line, or Pavel Dorofeyev will move back into the top-6 with Mitch Marner going back to centre. Head coach John Tortorella would not commit to his changes.

headline: Karlsson (upper-body) left Game 5 and is not likely to return for the remainder of the Stanley Cup Final.
McNabb (face) is expected to play in Game 4.
context: McNabb missed most of Game 2 after taking a slap shot off the face, but logged a massive 35:47 TOI in Game 3. McNabb missed Monday's practice but head coach John Tortorella said he expects the bruising defenseman to remain in the lineup for Game 4 on Tuesday. McNabb has been great for Vegas throughout the postseason, and comes into Game 4 with 33 blocked shots (7th most in the playoffs) and 34 hits (35th) to go along with nine points (1G / 8A) in 18 games.

headline: Hanifin (undisclosed) is expected to play in Game 4.
context: Hanifin left Game 3 in the second period after a hit from Jordan Martinook but eventually returned early in the third period. He missed practice on Monday but head coach John Tortorella said he expects Hanifin to play in Game 4 on Tuesday. Through 19 playoff games, Hanifin has picked up seven assists, 23 SOG, 19 hits and 40 blocked shots.

headline: McNabb (upper-body) is warming up and expected to play in Game 3 vs. Carolina.
context: Mcnabb could not finish Game 2 due to a scary upper-body injury but is warming up and expected to play Game 3 vs. Carolina. The 35-year-old is expected to wear a cage and return to his spot on Vegas' top defensive unit. In 17 playoff games this offseason, he has a goal, seven points and is a +10 plus/minus.

headline: McNabb (upper-body) left Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final and did not return.
Lauzon (undisclosed) will return for Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final.
context: Lauzon has not played since suffering an undisclosed injury in Game Six of Vegas' first-round series against the Utah Mammoth. He has been sidelined for over a month, but will return in Game One of the Stanley Cup Finals against the Carolina Hurricanes. The 29-year-old defenseman was averaging 16:33 time-on-ice and recorded eight blocks and 14 hits in six games before his injury. Kaedan Korczak will be a healthy scratch to accommodate Lauzon's return.

headline: Nichushkin (lower-body) will not play in Game 4 in Vegas.
context: Nichushkin exited Sunday's 5-3 Game Three loss to the Vegas Golden Knights in the second period after only playing 8:34 time-on-ice. The 31-year-old Nichushkin is the latest injury concern for an Avalanche team that has trouble staying healthy as they trail their third-round series 3-0. Nichushkin has four points (2G / 2A) in 12 games this postseason.

headline: MacKinnon (lower-body) will play in Game 4 in Vegas.
context: MacKinnon left Game Three on Sunday late in the second period after suffering a lower-body injury. He returned early in the third period, but was used sparingly, spending most of the final frame on the bench. It's unclear if he will be able to return to his usual playing capacity in Game Four, but his presence will nevertheless be a positive sign for an Avalanche team trying to stave off elimination.

The Avalanche had battled injuries in their third-round matchup against the Vegas Golden Knights and now, down 3-0, can ill-afford to be without their offensive superstar, MacKinnon.

context: Domi underwent surgery to address an issue he was dealing with throughout the 2025-26 season, but complications have arisen, making his availability for training camp uncertain. The 31-year-old forward scored 36 points (12G / 24A) and recorded a career-worst -29 plus/minus through 80 games last season.

context: Makar has missed the first two games of the Western Conference Final with an upper-body injury but is warming up and expected to return for Game 3 on Sunday. The 27-year-old superstar defensemen will make a welcome return as Colorado attempts to win its first game of the series. Makar has four goals, five points and +5 plus/minus in nine playoff games played thus far.

headline: Stone (undisclosed) will return for Game 3 vs. Colorado.
Stone (lower-body) will remain out vs. Colorado for Game 2.
context: Despite being a full participant in Friday's morning skate, Mark Stone will not return to Vegas' lineup for Game 2 vs. Colorado. Stone has not played since Game 3 of Vegas' previous series vs. Anaheim but seems on the cusp of returning in the upcoming games. The 34-year-old veteran has three goals, seven points and 18 SOG in nine games played so far this postseason.

headline: Makar (upper-body) will remain out for Game 2 vs. Vegas on Friday.
context: Makar was a full participant in Colorado's morning skate ahead of Game 2 but will remain out with an upper-body injury on Friday as the Avalanche host the Golden Knights. The 27-year-old superstar's absence creates a massive hole in Colorado's defence after he put up four goals and five points in their first nine playoff games while averaging 24:59 TOI.

headline: Helleson (groin strain) is expected to be ready for Training Camp.
context: Helleson played in eight of the Ducks' 12 postseason games but suffered a groin strain in Game 3 vs. the Golden Knights. He's expected to make a full recovery and be ready for training camp in the fall.

headline: Mintyukov (MCL sprain) is expected to be ready for Training Camp.
context: Mintyukov played through an MCL sprain throughout the postseason, failing to record a point in his 12 games. The Ducks expect him to be ready for training camp in the fall.

headline: Gauthier played through two broken vertebrae in April.
context: Gauthier broke his L1 and L2 vertebrae against the Maple Leafs on March 30th and played the final three games of the regular season and 12 playoff games. Gauthier is expected to be recovered fully for training camp in the fall. He'll look to build on a 41-goal breakout season in 2025-26.

headline: Terry played through a chronic hip impingement that will require surgery in the near future.
context: The Ducks managed Terry's hip injury down the stretch, giving him plenty of morning skates off towards the end of the regular season and throughout the postseason. They said that his surgery is planned for the "near future" but his timeline for return is to be determined. So consider him out indefinitely.

headline: Malinski (upper-body) will play in Game 1 against the Golden Knights.
context: Malinski missed Games 4 and 5 vs. the Wild but participated in Tuesday's practice and head coach Jared Bednar "hopes" to have Malinski and Artturi Lehkonen back in the lineup for Game 1 vs. Vegas on Wednesday. headline: Lehkonen (upper-body) will play in Game 1 against the Golden Knights.

context: Kulich suffered a blood clot in early November and was sidelined for the remainder of the 2025-26 season. That said, the Sabres received encouraging news that Kulich is trending in the right direction and is expected to return. The 22-year-old Czech forward, the 28th overall pick in the 2022 NHL Entry Draft, has 29 points (18G / 11A) in 75 career games.

headline: Gustavsson is having offseason hip surgery and is unsure if he’ll be ready for the start of the 2026-27 season.
context: Gustavsson was Minnesota's goalie-of-record during the 2025-26 regular season, starting 49 games, but dressed primarily as Jesper Wallstedt's backup during the team's postseason run. With Gustavsson undergoing offseason hip surgery, Jesper Wallstedt could be poised to make another push to be Minnesota's starting goalie to start the 2026-27 season. The 27-year-old Gustavsson will be entering the first year of a five-year contract extension worth $38 million ($6.8 million AAV).

headline: Power (undisclosed) will play in Game 6 in Montreal.
context: Power was nicked up in Game 5 and head coach Lindy Ruff said that he was receiving treatment on Friday for the undisclosed injury. On Saturday he said that Power is a "possibility" to play in the must-win Game 6 in Montreal. Power has picked up five assists in 11 playoff games so far.

headline: Stone (lower-body) will remain out for Game 6 in Anaheim.
context: Stone has not played the previous two games due to a lower-body injury, and will remain sidelined in Game Six. The Golden Knights are 1-1 this series without Stone, who is averaging 19:27 time-on-ice and has seven points (3G / 4A) in nine games this postseason.

headline: Lehkonen (upper-body) will not play in Game 5 against the Wild.
context: Lehkonen was a late scratch for Game 4 due to an upper-body injury but will be a game-time decision ahead of Game 5 vs. Minnesota on Wednesday. The 30-year-old has been a constant force in Colorado's electric top-six and has three goals, six points and a +9 plus/minus in seven playoff games this year.

headline: Malinski (upper-body) will not play in Game 5 against the Wild.
context: Malinski was an unexpected scratch for Game 4 with an upper-body injury but will now be a game-time decision as Colorado hosts Minnesota for Game 5 on Wednesday. The 27-year-old had a breakout campaign in 2026-26, with 40 points in 82 games and has continued that success into the postseason with an impressive three points and +7 plus/minus in 7 games played so far.

headline: Poehling (undisclosed) is out indefinitely.
context: Poehling was on the recieving end of a late, dirty hit by Vegas' Brayden McNabb and has been ruled out indefinitely by Head Coach Joel Quenneville on Wednesday. The 27-year-old forward's absence will create a large gap in Anaheim's lineup after he picked up four goals and five points throughout Anaheim's first 11 playoff games.

headline: White is week-to-week with an upper-body injury.

headline: Klingberg is day-to-day with an upper-body injury.

headline: Sturm is expected to be off the ice for four or five days due to back issues.

headline: Hague (upper-body is expected to miss the next 4-6 weeks.

headline: Benn is day-to-day with an upper-body injury.

headline: Batherson will miss the next two weeks with an upper-body injury.

headline: Benoit (upper-body) has yet to return to the ice with the Toronto Maple Leafs.

headline: Blomqvist is day-to-day with a lower-body injury.

headline: Ovechkin (lower body) skated on Tuesday and is expected to return in the upcoming days.

headline: Lee is out for 1 to 2 weeks with an upper-body injury.

headline: McBain is day-to-day with an undisclosed injury.

headline: Cooley is day-to-day with an undisclosed injury.

headline: Zuccarello could miss the start of the regular season with an undisclosed injury.

headline: Edvinsson is expected to be out for a few weeks with a lower-body injury.

headline: McCormick will not participate in training camp and is out indefinitely with a hip injury

headline: Girard (lower-body) is expected to miss part of training camp and is a possibility to return for opening night.

headline: Blackwood (lower-body) is week-to-week but is expected to be ready around the beginning of the season.

headline: Nosek (knee) suffered a significant injury while training and is expected to be out long-term.

headline: Nick Paul (upper-body) underwent surgery on Friday and is expected to miss the start of the season.

headline: Corey Perry successfully underwent knee surgery and is expected to miss the next 6-8 weeks.

headline: Pietrangelo (lower-body) is stepping away from hockey.
